clue.text: Expert way to cover half of Olympics

indicators.note: the way is wrapped around the other piece, covering it

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: only the first half of the word Olympics is used

explanation.surface: An expert pathway is being laid over part of an Olympic venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is a person of wide learning, an expert in many fields.

clue.text: Handing over additional information about a carol

indicators.note: about means the postscript goes round the a

parts.note: PS, postscript, adds information to a letter
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a postscript about a Christmas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing as a verb form means handing something on to another person.

clue.text: A lot of historical knowledge attached to railway truck

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge handed down

explanation.surface: A heap of history is hitched to a railway wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railway truck' reads as one thing; 'railway' belongs to the wordplay and 'truck' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry is the British word for a truck, a large goods vehicle.

clue.text: Power-crazed individual confused by a magical omen

indicators.note: confused means the following letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A would-be tyrant is thrown by a magical sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalomaniac is obsessed with power and their own importance.

clue.text: Giant bird heads for Alpine nest

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: heads means the first letters of Alpine and nest

explanation.surface: A huge bird makes for its nest in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giants of Greek myth, so a titan is anyone huge.

clue.text: Plans returning this unwanted correspondence

indicators.note: returning means the word for plans is read backwards

parts.note: maps are plans, as of a town or building

explanation.surface: Someone's plans come back to them as junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the name for unsolicited bulk email, mail nobody asked for.

clue.text: Peanut I fancy as a flowering plant

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a peanut plant as a flower for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a popular garden bedding plant with trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: One digs up some chrysanthemum in error

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener digs up some chrysanthemums by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner is a worker who excavates coal or ore from the ground.

clue.text: Cryptic shone fantastically: a spectacular display!

indicators.note: fantastically means wildly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cryptic clue shines brilliantly, putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrotechnics are fireworks, and by extension any dazzling show.

clue.text: Growing season, putting out new branch

indicators.note: putting out means the letter for new is ejected from the season

parts.note: spring is the season when plants grow

explanation.surface: In the growing season a plant puts out a new branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small twig or shoot, a little branch of a plant.

clue.text: Be audacious in the fitting-room?

definitions.meaning: in a fitting-room you try on clothes, literally trying it on

explanation.surface: Being bold while changing in a shop's fitting-room.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to test how much one can get away with; the literal sense is putting on a garment to check it fits.

clue.text: Hot, with sources of some peppers removed, implies cold

indicators.note: removed means those letters are taken out of the word for hot

parts.note: hot food is spicy

indicators.note: sources are beginnings, so the first letters of some and peppers are taken

explanation.surface: Taking the seeds out of a few chillies makes the dish cool rather than hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' looks like temperature, but it is the spicy sense; the result, its opposite, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy is a synonym of very cold, as of frozen weather.

clue.text: Farmer, maybe, having unhappy experience with computer network

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: A farmer has a bad time with the office computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer is one example of a person who owns land, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Poorly-lit weaving machine blocking outside of gallery

indicators.note: blocking means the machine sits between and stops up the other letters
outside of means the first and last letters of gallery

parts.note: a loom is the machine for weaving cloth

explanation.surface: A loom stands in a gallery entrance in a dim exhibition space.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy can mean dark or dimly lit, as a gloomy corridor.

clue.text: Old Emperor taking on America, implying a lot of work

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
US stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An ancient emperor taking on the United States would be a big job.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous describes a task that is burdensome and demands great effort.

clue.text: Prize in conflict secured by Communist

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the other word

parts.note: a Red is a communist
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A medal won in war is handed out by a Communist regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in recognition, such as a prize.

clue.text: Dictionary includes "beer" as local usage

indicators.note: includes means the beer goes inside the dictionary word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A dictionary lists the word 'beer' as a regionalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a form of language peculiar to one region.

clue.text: Riotous cheering around Western part of London

indicators.note: around means the scrambled word is placed about the letter for western
riotous suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Wild cheers from a crowd somewhere in West London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riotous' turns CHEERING into GREENICH; 'around' puts that about W.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is a borough in south-east London, home of the Royal Observatory and the prime meridian.

clue.text: Doctor penning article: editor looked astonished

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the article goes inside

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a doctor
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A doctor writes a piece and the editor is stunned.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed in wonder.

clue.text: Church in urban area losing head, getting irritated

indicators.note: in means the church goes inside the shortened word
losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a city is an urban area

explanation.surface: A city church loses its leader and the congregation gets annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church in urban area' reads as one place, but the church is the piece placed inside, and 'losing head' trims the urban area before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy describes skin with an irritating sensation needing a scratch.

clue.text: Bath, say, having reduced width

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: span is the width across something, as of a bridge

explanation.surface: The city of Bath is narrower than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath, the English city famous for Roman hot springs, is an example of a spa town; 'say' signals the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs, of which Bath is the classic English instance.

clue.text: Industrial waste receiving name in informal language

indicators.note: receiving means taking the letter for name inside

parts.note: slag is the waste left from smelting

explanation.surface: A slag heap is given a nickname in colloquial speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is very informal vocabulary, outside standard speech.

clue.text: Dull photo with flowery girl in it

indicators.note: in it means the girl goes inside the photo

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
Rosa is a girl's name and the Latin for a rose, so flowery

explanation.surface: A boring snapshot shows a girl in a floral dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means unimaginative and ordinary, lacking poetic spark.

clue.text: One million going to a good European picture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A million is paid to a decent European for a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or picture of something.

clue.text: Remains of the French Saint

parts.note: du is French for of the

explanation.surface: The relics of a French saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust is what is left of a body after decay, as in 'dust to dust'.

clue.text: Vision certainly possessed by rowing crew

indicators.note: possessed by means held within the crew word

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes means certainly as an answer

explanation.surface: A rowing crew certainly has good vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, synonymous with vision.
